description: Close out the Appian plug-in policy sweep and the documentation the rename invalidated: fix the one unclosed Closeable and the one factually false SDK Javadoc claim, confirm the Java 17 toolchain, and make targeted fixes to docs/mqtt-plugin-guide.md and the empty info.md. The sweep itself is already almost entirely clean - this feature fixes the two real findings and records the rest as report evidence. Depends on FEAT-001 (file paths and package names) and FEAT-002 (the META-INF/lib and single-artifact facts the docs must state). Implements items 11-13 and 15 of .agents/tasks/appmarket-compliance-plan.md.
steps: Fix the one unclosed Closeable: in src/main/java/de/hock/mqtt/template/MqttConnectedSystemTemplate.java, method resolveDocumentBytes(...) (~line 517) does java.io.InputStream in = doc.getInputStream(); reads it with readAllBytes(), and never closes it. Convert to try-with-resources while preserving the existing behavior exactly: a null stream still returns null early, an empty byte array still returns null, and java.io.IOException is still swallowed with return null so resolution falls through to the runtime layer.

Correct the false SDK claim in the same file's class Javadoc, which states there is no SimpleConnectedSystemTemplate in this SDK version. That is wrong - SimpleConnectedSystemTemplate lives in com.appian:connected-systems-client, an artifact this pom does not declare. Reword to say accurately that the plug-in deliberately uses the low-level ConnectedSystemTemplate interface and that the Simple* hierarchy would require the undeclared connected-systems-client dependency. Do not replace it with any new unverified claim, and DO NOT migrate to the Simple* base classes or add that dependency - that migration is explicitly out of scope.

Optionally wrap the two new ByteArrayInputStream(...) uses in try-with-resources for strict policy cleanliness: src/main/java/de/hock/mqtt/validation/CertificateLoader.java ~line 138 and src/main/java/de/hock/mqtt/protocol/ConnectOptionsFactory.java ~line 193. Neither holds an OS resource, so behavior is unchanged.

Confirm the Java 17 toolchain and change nothing: pom.xml already sets <maven.compiler.release>17</maven.compiler.release> and maven-compiler-plugin consumes it via <release>. release supersedes source/target, so do NOT add redundant maven.compiler.source or maven.compiler.target properties. Confirm with the javap 'major version: 61' check.

Re-run and record the policy sweep as report evidence (no code change expected): grep -rn 'System\.out\|System\.err\|printStackTrace\|java\.util\.logging\|System\.setProperty\|java\.io\.File\|java\.nio\.file' src/main/java must return no matches. Facts to state in findings: there is NO logging framework in the project at all, so nothing routes anywhere and there is nothing to re-route to Log4j - do not invent a logging stack; TLS is built as an in-memory SSLContext and handed to Paho via options.setSocketFactory(...) in ConnectOptionsFactory, i.e. the compliant pattern, with zero System.setProperty; CertificateLoader parses certificates and PKCS#8 keys purely from byte arrays, so there are NO temp keystore files and no filesystem access anywhere; the only password/keyPassphrase literals are field-key name constants in ConfigFields, not credentials; there are no SNAPSHOT versions.

Make targeted doc fixes only - do NOT rewrite docs/mqtt-plugin-guide.md wholesale. In its 'Build and install' section (~lines 196-210): state that the nested Paho jar is bundled under META-INF/lib/ rather than lib/, and state unambiguously that target/mqtt-broker-connected-system-1.0.0-plugin.jar is the artifact to deploy and submit. Drop the now-obsolete sentence warning against deploying the plain jar, since FEAT-002 stops it being built - keep that warning only if FEAT-002's findings record that it ended on the fallback path. Also re-grep the guide for com.appian.mqtt and any stale plug-in key and fix whatever the rename invalidated.

info.md is 0 bytes - give it a short AppMarket-facing summary: plug-in name, key de.hock.mqtt, vendor Hock, version 1.0.0.0, minimum Appian 26.9.0.0, the connected system plus its two integrations (publish = WRITE, subscribe = READ), and the bundled Eclipse Paho 1.2.5 with its EDL-1.0 license. Keep it brief; do not pad it.
acceptance_criteria: mvn -q clean package succeeds and mvn test reports Tests run: 3, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0
No InputStream obtained from doc.getInputStream() is left unclosed in MqttConnectedSystemTemplate.java - the read happens inside a try-with-resources
MqttConnectedSystemTemplate.java no longer claims that SimpleConnectedSystemTemplate does not exist in this SDK version
javap -verbose on a class unzipped from the shipped jar reports 'major version: 61'
grep -rn 'com\.appian\.mqtt' docs info.md returns no matches, and docs/mqtt-plugin-guide.md names META-INF/lib/ and the exact submission artifact filename
verification: export JAVA_HOME=/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/amazon-corretto-17.jdk/Contents/Home && cd /Users/andreas.hock/Documents/Appian-Projects/MQTT_Component && mvn -q clean package && mvn test 2>&1 | grep -E 'Tests run|BUILD'

cd /tmp && rm -rf jarchk && mkdir jarchk && cd jarchk && unzip -o -q /Users/andreas.hock/Documents/Appian-Projects/MQTT_Component/target/mqtt-broker-connected-system-1.0.0-plugin.jar 'de/hock/mqtt/template/MqttConnectedSystemTemplate.class' && javap -verbose de/hock/mqtt/template/MqttConnectedSystemTemplate.class | grep 'major version' && cd /tmp && rm -rf jarchk
findings:
DONE. All steps implemented in place; no git command was run. Network was available - no 'mvn -o' fallback needed. Scope held: no Simple* migration, no connected-systems-client dependency, no SDK version change, no logging framework introduced, no new tests, docs/mqtt-plugin-guide.md edited only at the two named spots.

BUILD/TEST EVIDENCE (export JAVA_HOME=.../amazon-corretto-17.jdk/Contents/Home): 'mvn -q clean package' succeeded, then 'mvn test' -> 'Tests run: 3, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0, Time elapsed: 0.025 s -- in de.hock.mqtt.ProjectStructureTest', 'Tests run: 3, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0', BUILD SUCCESS. 'ls target/*.jar' -> exactly one file, target/mqtt-broker-connected-system-1.0.0-plugin.jar (FEAT-002's phase-none path holds). 'jar tf ... | grep -c .java$' -> 33, unchanged.

CODE FIX 1 (unclosed Closeable, src/main/java/de/hock/mqtt/template/MqttConnectedSystemTemplate.java, resolveDocumentBytes, now ~line 518-531): converted to try-with-resources. getInputStream() is still called EXACTLY ONCE into a local 'documentStream' (calling it twice inside the condition could have opened and leaked a second stream), the null stream still returns null before any try block, the stream is then resourced as 'try (java.io.InputStream in = documentStream)', an empty byte[] still returns null, and java.io.IOException is still swallowed with 'return null' so resolution falls through to the runtime layer. Behavior is byte-for-byte identical apart from the close. 'grep -n getInputStream' on the file now returns a single line, 520.

CODE FIX 2 (false SDK claim, same file, class Javadoc lines ~40-45): removed '(there is no SimpleConnectedSystemTemplate in this SDK version)'. Replacement states that the plug-in deliberately implements the low-level ConnectedSystemTemplate interface and that the Simple* template hierarchy (e.g. SimpleConnectedSystemTemplate) ships in the separate com.appian:connected-systems-client artifact which this pom does not declare. No new unverified claim was added; no migration was performed and that dependency was NOT added.

STEP 3 (optional ByteArrayInputStream wrapping) DELIBERATELY NOT DONE, and this is a judgement call worth reviewing: ByteArrayInputStream holds no OS resource and its close() is a no-op, but it inherits 'throws IOException' from InputStream, so try-with-resources at CertificateLoader.parseCertificate (~line 138) would force an extra 'catch (java.io.IOException)' arm that can never fire - dead defensive code in a method whose only catch today is CertificateException. ConnectOptionsFactory.buildTrustManagers (~line 193) already catches java.io.IOException, so it would be free there, but wrapping one and not the other is worse than wrapping neither. The step was explicitly optional with 'behavior is unchanged', so both sites were left as-is. No policy requirement is violated: the AppMarket Closeable rule targets resources that hold handles.

STEP 4 TOOLCHAIN - CONFIRMED, NOTHING CHANGED: pom.xml line 17 '<maven.compiler.release>17</maven.compiler.release>', line 87 maven-compiler-plugin 3.13.0 consuming '<release>${maven.compiler.release}</release>'. No maven.compiler.source or maven.compiler.target was added (release supersedes them). Proof from the SHIPPED jar: unzipped de/hock/mqtt/template/MqttConnectedSystemTemplate.class out of target/mqtt-broker-connected-system-1.0.0-plugin.jar, 'javap -verbose' -> 'major version: 61' (Java 17).

POLICY SWEEP RE-RUN - CLEAN, NO CODE CHANGE NEEDED. Command: grep -rn 'System\.out\|System\.err\|printStackTrace\|java\.util\.logging\|System\.setProperty\|java\.io\.File\|java\.nio\.file' src/main/java -> NO MATCHES ('SWEEP CLEAN'). Supporting greps and the facts they establish:
  - LOGGING: 'grep -rni log4j|slf4j|logback|Logger pom.xml src/main/java' -> NO MATCHES. There is NO logging framework in the project at all. Nothing is logged anywhere, so there is nothing to re-route to Log4j and no Log4j stack was invented. Error information travels as return values: ValidationResult/ValidationResults at design time and the diagnostics package (Redactor, ResponseMapper, ExceptionCategoryTranslator, DiagnosticsBuilder) at runtime.
  - TLS: zero System.setProperty anywhere. TLS is built as an in-memory SSLContext in ConnectOptionsFactory and handed to Paho via options.setSocketFactory(...) - the compliant pattern, no JVM-global mutation.
  - FILESYSTEM: zero java.io.File and zero java.nio.file references in src/main/java. CertificateLoader parses X.509 certificates and PKCS#8 keys purely from byte arrays via CertificateFactory/PKCS8EncodedKeySpec over ByteArrayInputStream; the KeyStore instances in ConnectOptionsFactory are loaded with load(null, null), i.e. in memory. There are NO temp keystore files and no filesystem access anywhere, so there is nothing to delete.
  - CREDENTIALS: the only password / keyPassphrase literals are field-KEY NAME constants in de.hock.mqtt.validation.ConfigFields, not credentials. Secrets are declared with EncryptedTextPropertyDescriptor, held in char[], and redacted by diagnostics/Redactor.
  - VERSIONS: 'grep -rni SNAPSHOT pom.xml' -> NO MATCHES ('NO SNAPSHOTS'). All plugin and dependency versions are pinned via properties.

DOC CHANGES (targeted only, guide NOT rewritten - 2 hunks, 220 lines otherwise untouched):
  - docs/mqtt-plugin-guide.md 'Build and install' (~line 204-209): replaced the sentence that said the jar bundles Paho under 'lib/' and warned against deploying the plain jar. It now states that the build produces exactly ONE jar in target/, that target/mqtt-broker-connected-system-1.0.0-plugin.jar is the artifact to deploy and to submit to the AppMarket, that Paho is nested under META-INF/lib/ because that is where Appian's plug-in classloader resolves nested jars, and that the jar carries its own .java sources beside the classes. The 'not the plain mqtt-broker-connected-system-1.0.0.jar' warning was DROPPED, which is correct per FEAT-002's findings: FEAT-002 ended on the phase-none primary path, not the documented fallback, so the plain jar is no longer built at all and 'ls target/*.jar' confirms a single artifact.
  - docs/mqtt-plugin-guide.md header (line 10-11): '**Minimum Appian version:** 18.4.0.0' was stale against the manifest FEAT-002 rewrote; corrected to 26.9.0.0 and a '**Plug-in key:** de.hock.mqtt' line added so the guide names the key the manifest now carries.
  - Re-grep of the guide for the rename: 'grep -rn com\.appian\.mqtt docs info.md' -> NO MATCHES ('DOCS CLEAN'), and no stale plug-in key string survived; nothing else in the guide referenced the old package or key.
  - info.md was 0 bytes and is now a short AppMarket-facing summary (~25 lines, not padded): plug-in name, key de.hock.mqtt, vendor Hock, version 1.0.0.0, minimum Appian 26.9.0.0, the MQTT Broker connected system, both integrations with their request policies (Publish = WRITE, Subscribe = READ), and the bundled Eclipse Paho 1.2.5 under EDL-1.0 pointing at THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md.

ALL 7 ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA CONFIRMED: build+3/3 tests green; the doc.getInputStream() read is inside try-with-resources; the 'no SimpleConnectedSystemTemplate in this SDK version' claim is gone; the policy sweep grep returns no matches; javap on the class from the shipped jar reports major version 61; docs/info.md are free of com.appian.mqtt and the guide names META-INF/lib/ plus the exact submission filename; info.md is no longer empty.

STILL OPEN FOR THE USER (carried from FEAT-002, not fixable here): the vendor URL https://hock.de in src/main/resources/appian-plugin.xml is still a placeholder assumption and must be replaced with the real one before submission - Appian reviewers check that it resolves. No connected-system logo PNG exists under src/main/resources (needs artwork). META-INF/lib nested-jar resolution can only be proven by one deploy cycle on a real Appian 26.9 instance.
